_about: The sky the original pins to the camera: StaticSky, in Sky.angelscript. Decoded from
android_game.bin through the remake's asbc listing (all_functions.txt, md5
48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0; the excerpt Step 44 read is kept at the remake's
A level places its sky where the level editor left it, and the original overwrites that
on every frame: the sky is drawn centred on the screen and one screen tall, whatever the
camera does. The port drew it where the level put it, and on 34 levels the camera moved
off it onto black (step 44's bare-ground census).
MEASURED ON THE ORIGINAL, not only read: on 16 of 16 library levels the original draws
its sky at the screen's centre to within 1 px, whatever its camera did (static_sky's

_source: Game::preLoop (Game.angelscript, bytes 112536..114414), instructions 148-182: if
Game.spaceBg, SpaceSky(); else StaticSky(sceneMax.x, 'sky', true). The controller is
added after the camera's, the portal manager's and the earthquake's (281-287), so it
reads the camera this frame left. Game.spaceBg is false by Game::Game (instruction
328) and set by Game::readProperties (116676..118260, 149-164) when the first
`properties` entity carries `space_bg` at all: CheckCustomData != 0, whatever it
holds. sceneMax.x is passed and never read.
StaticSky::StaticSky (153461..153922): GetEntityArray(name) and GetEntityArray(name +
'.ent') into m_skies - entity names 'sky' and 'sky.ent', matched exactly
(ETHBucketManager::GetEntityArrayByName, ETHBucketManager.cpp:488-503, an == on the
name) - then scaleSky(); then, handleSatellite being
true, m_satellite = SeekEntity('satellite') and, when found, its `originalPos` = its
own GetPositionXY().
StaticSky::scaleSky (154161..154942), for each sky t: skyScale = GetScreenSize().y /
GetSize().y and Scale(skyScale); m_width = GetSize().x after it; m_scrollValue =
GetFloat('scroll'); m_scroll = m_scrollValue > 0 (CMPIf 0, TP); position(t);
scrollPos = (0, 0); and for a scrolling sky SetPivotAdjust(size * (1, 0)) when t is 0
and SetPivotAdjust(size * (-1, 0)) when t is the last - `size` being the size BEFORE
the scale, and the second call replacing the first on a lone sky. The unscaled size is
what moves the picture: SetPivotAdjust stores p / GetScale() (ETHEntity.cpp:1019-1022)
and the draw subtracts pivotAdjust * scale from the position: an unrotated sky is
drawn by ETHSpriteEntity::GetScreenRect (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:742-752), less
ETHEntity::ComputeAbsoluteOrigin (ETHEntity.cpp:270-297), which adds pivotAdjust *
scale; the rotated branch (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:702-708) gives the same centre. m_width,
m_scroll and m_scrollValue are one member each, so the last sky's stand for all.
StaticSky::position (154942..155688): size = GetSize(); pitch = size * 0.5; if not
m_scroll, pitch = GetScreenSize() * 0.5; else pitch.x += size.x when t is 0 and
pitch.x -= size.x when t is the last. originalPos = pitch + (m_width * t, 0);
SetPositionXY(GetCameraPos() + originalPos + scrollPos). GetCameraPos() is the
screen's top-left corner, the video camera's position (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:
350-356; dragon.json's camera note).
StaticSky::update (155688..156307): scrollMove = scaledUnitsPerSecond(-m_scrollValue);
for each sky position(t), then, if m_scroll, scrollPos += (scrollMove, 0) and
scrollPos = (0, 0) once abs(scrollPos.x) >= m_width. Then the satellite, when there is
one: SetPositionXY(GetCameraPos() + its originalPos).
screen_pitch is the 0.5 literal (position, instructions 18 and 32). frame_cap_ms is
STimeManager::unitsPerSecond's min(200, GetLastFrameElapsedTime())
(STimeManager.angelscript, 8045..8162), which scaledUnitsPerSecond (8284..8363)
multiplies by g_scale: a speed in the level's own units, as the port counts them.
Checked in the remake's out/parity/specs/ui3/work/motion/dec_state.txt: instructions 5-9
push 200, call GetLastFrameElapsedTime and min; the result is speed * that / a double
constant (read as ms to seconds) * m_factor, which STimeManager's constructor sets to 1
and pause() / resume() set to 0 / 1. The scroll branch no level reaches would therefore
also stop while the original is paused.
_units: GetScreenSize() and GetSize() are screen pixels in the original, and every entity was
multiplied by g_scale = screen.y / 256 first (SGlobalScale::scaleEntities, preLoop
instruction 37; main.angelscript's preLoop sets the 256). In the level's own units the
scale is therefore view height / picture height: 256 / 256 = 1 for every sky the levels
place, whose pictures are all 256 u tall at every tier (1x 455x256, fullhd 1024x512 at
density 2). So the port changes where a sky is drawn and not its size.
The fullhd tiers of sky, icy_sky, red_sky and sky_purple are 1024 x 512 texels whose
outer 57 columns each side are (0, 0, 0): 455 u of picture inside 512 at density 2,
with the black 28.5 u each side (the remake's out/parity/visuals/sky/fix2/
fullhd_padding.txt); satellite_sky is 512 u in both tiers. The 1x file is not that
picture at 1:1 on two of them (out/parity/visuals/sky/verify3/tier_geom.txt and
tier_geom2.txt): 1x sky.png is the whole fullhd image resampled to about 554 x 277 and
cropped (NCC 0.9990, against 0.8717 at 1:1), a content scale of 1.082 whose inverse,
0.924, is the visuals plan's gap D 0.9275, and 3.5 apart per pixel after a per-channel
gain and offset, a grade; red_sky is about 1.047x (NCC 0.9751 against 0.9080) and 9.4
apart after that fit; icy_sky and sky_purple are 1:1 (NCC 1.0000 and 0.9970). That
picture tier, content scale and grade, is the visuals plan's System 6, not this step's
_measured: Where the ORIGINAL draws its sky, on its own library frames (the remake's
out/parity/original/levels/<W-LL>_t8.0.png, 1280 x 720): the remake's
out/parity/visuals/sky/where_orig_sky.py slides the sky picture of the tier the original
draws (fullhd 512x256 u or 1x 455x256 u) over the frame and keeps the centre where the
most pixels agree. Results: out/parity/visuals/sky/where_orig_sky.txt (10 levels),
verify/where_orig_extra.txt (5 more) and fix2/where_orig_1-13.txt (1-13).
1-01 at (640, 359): 184,357 px agree there, 183,431 at the centre.
2-03 at (640, 361): 529,136 px agree there, 529,132 at the centre.
1-13 at (641, 360) at t8.0 and h6.3: 101,052 px agree there, 100,890 at the centre.
That is 16 of 16 at the screen's centre to within 1 px, including 1-01, whose level puts
its sky 2 u right and 8 u up of that, 2-01 and 4-32, whose cameras have scrolled 57 and
313 u, and 2-05 and 1-13, whose cameras have scrolled 44 and 88 u down. screen_pitch
0.5 is this.
Not scrolling, on the original's frames: the band y 0..199, x 150..599 of 3-05 and of
3-06, both scrolling_sky levels, differs by 0 at most between h2.8 and h6.3 (one run,
3.5 s apart) and between t4.5 and t8.0 (another). On 3-05 that band is all sky (100% of
it within 10 of satellite_sky pinned at the centre); on 3-06 70.3% is sky and the rest
scenery, so 3-05 is the level that shows the sky itself still.
_census: Over the 128 converted levels (tests/test_mp_sky.cpp pins it): 95 place exactly one
sky (93 named 'sky', 2 'sky.ent'), so t is 0 on every level and m_width never moves a
drawn pixel; 19 set space_bg and place `space_sky` instead; 13 place neither; one,
level14b (3-15), places a `satellite` and no sky.
NO SKY SCROLLS. No level's sky carries a `scroll` variable - not one of the 133 .esc
files and none of the sky .ent files has <Name>scroll</Name> - and GetFloat answers 0
for a missing name (ETHEntity.cpp:851-856). The `scrolling_sky` = 1 that 37 levels'
`properties` entity carries is a different variable, and the string 'scrolling_sky'
occurs nowhere in the listing's 1,473 functions, where every other properties key the
levels use is read. The original's own frames agree: in 3-05, a scrolling_sky level,
a band that is all sky (y 0..199, x 150..599) is identical to the byte in h2.8 and
h6.3, one run 3.5 s apart, and in t4.5 and t8.0 of another (3-06's same band, 70% sky,
is as still); a scroll of 1 u/s would have moved it 10 px. The scroll branch is carried
and tested as decoded; no shipped level reaches it.

_not_ported: The 19 space_bg levels (4-01 to 4-19) build SpaceSky instead (Sky.angelscript,
SpaceSky::SpaceSky 156379..157122 and ::update 157259..158171), which is outside step
44's excerpt and NOT ported here. What the full listing shows: it seeks
`planet_bg.ent`, `spiral`, `space_sky` and `eclipse.ent`; the spiral is scaled to the
screen's diagonal (scaleToSize), coloured by its `alpha` (0.7 when absent), pinned to
camera + screen * (0.5, 1) and turned by unitsPerSecond(-1.7) a frame; space_sky is
pinned to camera + screen * 0.5 at its own size; the planet gets speed 0.5 and stride 1
and runs linearMotion from camera + screen * (0.5, 1) each frame; the eclipse is placed
at camera + (screen.x * 0.5, its own y). Porting it needs linearMotion
329349..329538) read as well: both are in the listing, not yet read. Step 44 counted
no bare ground on these levels.
